Thanks for taking a look at this quickly. Attached is our redline of the proposed amendment. Two items to flag:

- We asked to split the SOW into Core Inference (Exhibit D-1) and Premium Support (Exhibit D-2) so we can phase the rollout. The redline shows suggested text.
- Our procurement team (copied) is asking for a harmonized rate schedule — we want to avoid separate rate tables per exhibit. We proposed a single rate ladder but highlighted the band for Premium Support.

Can Redwood confirm whether a single Exhibit with subsectioning vs. two Exhibits is easier for legal to track? We also have internal approval deadlines next Wednesday (2026-10-21) so if we can get a legal turn within 48 hours, that would help.

Steph / Marta — reviewed the redline. High-level comments:

1) Traceability: single Exhibit with clear subsections (D.1 / D.2 headings inside Exhibit D) is preferable. This keeps the order form footprint smaller and avoids two separate exhibit signature artifacts.
2) Rate table: we can accept a consolidated rate ladder. I recommend a single table with a new column "Support Band" that maps lines to Core vs Premium. This preserves a single pricing schedule while making reconciliation explicit.
3) Acceptance language: Helix's proposed acceptance criteria in section 3.2 needs a small amendment to avoid creating an unbounded test period. I'll mark text to set a 30-day acceptance window per deliverable.

I've attached an annotated clause map with inline notes and a short redline for the acceptance clause. If we go with a single Exhibit, legal can produce a clean amendment word doc for signature. If Helix insists on two exhibits, we'll need an ops mapping doc.

Attachments: SOW_clause-map_laura_comments.xlsx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
